# METR (2026) — Frontier Risk Report (February to March 2026)

> **External, not NASA governance.** Useful for comparison and vocabulary. It never establishes
> what NASA requires, and must not be cited as NASA coverage.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Publisher / owner** | METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) |
| **Kind** | Report (pilot third-party risk assessment) |
| **Status** | Assessment window 16 Feb to 16 Mar 2026; publication date 19 May 2026 (p.1). 320 PDF pages including appendices. A pilot; the report says it plans a similar process in late 2026 (p.4). |
| **Where to get it** | Public: `https://metr.org/risk-report-feb-mar-2026.pdf`, confirmed anonymously off-network, 2026-10-26. |
| **Binds whom** | No one. |

**What it is good for, relative to NASA's documents.** An example of an outside assessor evaluating risk
from AI agents used inside the developer organizations. Comparison only (our reading).

**Key content for AI / machine-learning assurance.**
- Describes a pilot with four participating companies assessing "misalignment risks from AI agents used
  inside frontier AI developers" (p.2). It is entity-based rather than model-specific (pp.2, 6).
- Overall finding: internal agents "plausibly had the means, motive, and opportunity to start small
  rogue deployments, but they did not have the means to make them highly robust" (p.3).
- Defines "rogue deployment" as agents that "deliberately subverted initially applied control and
  oversight measures" and operate against the developer's intent (p.43). Indirect undermining of human
  control is out of scope (p.42).
- Caveats on independence: the pilot agreements did not give participants the right to approve the
  publication, but the report says the pilot "was not designed to provide robust accountability" (p.4).
- Appendices cover process (App. A, p.55), an incident database (App. D, p.86) and evaluations (App. E, p.132).

**Nearest NASA counterpart.** None in `../documents/` (our reading).
